staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable H3 checkout. Its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer trace: the overflowing write is at `src/h3lib/lib/polyfill.c:720` and the caller allocation is at `src/apps/fuzzers/fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles.c:35`. ARVO metadata names later commit `7268098e83fd3fc571dd96441ce7a702c8fd8e76` as vulnerable; this GT follows the live staged source and saved crash artifacts.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 375220555 (h3): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 found by fuzz target fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/375220555
bug_description.normalized: The staged 81-byte witness is interpreted by the fuzzer as resolution `1` and five raw `LatLng` vertices, then sent through every containment mode. On the crashing `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` arm, `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental()` first estimates how many `H3Index` slots are needed, but it forcibly switches the internal compact iterator to `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX` before counting candidate cells. That estimate is then used unchanged to allocate the caller's heap buffer. `polygonToCellsExperimental()` later fills the same buffer using the original `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode, where the `cellBoundaryCrossesPolygon` inclusion path is active, so it can emit more cells than the earlier BBOX-mode estimate counted. In the reproduced run the saved allocation size proves the estimate was 70 slots, while the saved differential evidence shows the vulnerable write index reaches `i == 70`; with no live capacity argument or enforced bound check in the vulnerable API, `out[i++] = iter.cell` stores the 71st element exactly one `H3Index` past the 560-byte heap region and triggers the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow.

evidence_note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace fixes the sink at `polyfill.c:720` and the allocation site at `fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles.c:35`. The repair context contributes previously validated runtime measurements for this same staged package: vulnerable side `sz == 70` and `i == 70` at the overflowing write, fixed side `size == 76` and final write index `75`, plus unchanged propagation of the caller buffer into the sink. This Stage 02 package preserves those measured facts while moving scored anchors onto project code in `src/h3lib/lib/polyfill.c`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-shaped polygon, resolution, and containment mode into the iterator state later used by the vulnerable estimate/fill mismatch.
source.value_from: The staged witness is exactly 81 bytes. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, byte 0 becomes `res = 1` and the remaining 80 bytes are reinterpreted as five `LatLng` vertices, then reused across the containment loop. The saved sanitizer stack and the staged regression test `src/apps/testapps/testPolygonToCellsReportedExperimental.c` both ground the crashing path in the overlapping mode that is passed into this library initializer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This accumulation materializes the caller-visible output-capacity estimate from the compact iterator's accepted cells. On the reproduced run, the later 560-byte allocation proves the final total returned through `&sz` was 70 slots.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. After 70 in-bounds writes fill indices `0..69` of the caller's 70-slot heap buffer, the next overlapping-mode cell is written as `out[70]`, exactly one `H3Index` past the allocation.

root_cause.description: The estimator overwrites the caller's requested containment mode with `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`, so the size count is computed under a narrower acceptance rule than the later overlapping fill. That underestimation is the project statement that creates the unsafe state consumed at the sink.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-shaped polygon survives iterator initialization and does not take the early error return, so the estimator reaches the flag rewrite and counting loop.

allocator_reached.description: On the crashing arm, the estimate call returns `E_SUCCESS` with `sz < MAX_SZ`, so `run()` proceeds into `calloc(sz, sizeof(H3Index))` and then calls the vulnerable fill function with that buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The first project-code consumption of the attacker-shaped state creates the compact iterator from the fuzzed polygon geometry, `res = 1`, and the overlapping containment mode selected by the harness loop.

Root-cause step. The estimator discards the caller's requested `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode and rewrites the iterator to `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`, changing the later size count to a different acceptance rule.

On the estimate path, the boundary-crossing inclusion branch is disabled because step 2 changed `mode` away from `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`. Cells that would be admitted only by this overlap-specific test are therefore omitted from the size count.

The estimator accumulates the compact iterator's accepted cells into the caller-visible slot count. The saved 560-byte allocation at the caller proves the final returned total was `sz == 70` on the crashing run.

The caller allocates exactly the estimated number of `H3Index` slots. Because `H3Index` is 8 bytes and AddressSanitizer reports a 560-byte region, this allocation created a 70-element buffer at `[0x516000000980,0x516000000bb0)`.

The fill function reinitializes iteration with the real caller-supplied `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode and starts writing at `i = 0`, but the vulnerable signature receives only `out`, not the caller's capacity. In the reproduced build the optional `H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS_ASSERT` guard was not active, or the later overflowing write would have been stopped first.

On the actual fill path, the same overlap-specific boundary-crossing branch is active because `mode` is now the original `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`. This allows the iterator to produce at least one cell that was not counted in the BBOX-mode estimate.

Sink. The saved differential measurements show the vulnerable execution reaches this write with `i == 70` while the caller buffer from step 5 has only 70 slots. The store therefore writes `out[70]`, which AddressSanitizer reports as an 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow exactly 0 bytes past the 560-byte allocation.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds a `size` parameter to `polygonToCellsExperimental` and returns `E_MEMORY_BOUNDS` when `i >= size` before the write. Stage 02 did not rerun fixed validation; this source-level note is supported by the patch diff and preserved repair-context measurements.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at `polygonToCellsExperimental /src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/polyfill.c:720:18`, which is the fine-trace sink step.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_patch: Yes at the source level. The fix both passes caller capacity into `polygonToCellsExperimental` and enforces `i < size` before `out[i++]`, addressing the estimate-to-write mismatch exposed here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged 81-byte `poc` to `fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at `polyfill.c:720`.

format.name: raw H3 polygon-to-cells no-holes fuzz buffer
format.contract: Exact staged witness only: an 81-byte buffer whose first byte is `0x01`, so the harness uses `res = 1`, and whose remaining 80 bytes are reinterpreted as five raw `LatLng` vertices with no holes. On the overlapping containment arm, this exact geometry leads the estimator to return 70 output slots while the real fill path attempts at least one additional `H3Index` write, so `out[70]` lands at the first byte past the 560-byte allocation.
